contract: design-contract.md; product requirements FR-09 and demonstration specification section 8. Screenshots in this directory render controlled synthetic browser API fixtures, not actual MCP execution evidence.

accessibility.evidence: Chromium UI fixture suite passed axe WCAG 2 A/AA and 2.1 A/AA scans on empty chat at both target widths. Keyboard tests verified the skip link, page focus, mobile drawer initial focus and Escape restoration. Reduced-motion loading spinner was verified to have animation-name none. Source inspection confirms mobile 44px controls and visible focus. This is a scoped automated check, not a complete accessibility certification.

responsive.evidence: Browser assertions found no document-level horizontal overflow at 390x844 and 1440x900 for empty and long-response states. Both widths were captured and inspected with view_image. Mobile navigation uses an inert background and focus trap; activity becomes a separate panel. Conversation scrolling preserves the composer.

loading.evidence: A delayed synthetic session response visibly showed Opening your workspace; reduced-motion styling was checked in the browser.

empty.evidence: Empty chat shows concrete prompt actions and connector status. An empty approvals page visibly explains that no action is awaiting review.

error.evidence: A failed synthetic POST shows the backend error without retrying a write automatically. Actual mock backend PDF validation failure also appeared as failed with prior completed tool calls preserved.

partial.evidence: Persisted partial-response fixture retained available Gmail content and explicitly disclosed unavailable Calendar/Drive data and stopped execution.

success.evidence: Controlled synthetic response fixtures and the actual mock backend both rendered sourced report output and validated artifact cards. The real browser flow downloaded a generated artifact, asserted all three Google source providers plus four MCP server namespaces, and restored saved conversation history.

permission.evidence: Fixtures verified exact recipients/body, one approval decision, expired action disablement, and Google-only sign-in in live mode. Actual mock backend browser tests passed both rejection and separate create-draft/send approvals with exactly two approval IDs and one send trace.

renderedEvidence.observation: Rendered mobile empty workspace: visible synthetic label, concrete prompt controls, fixed composer, responsive navigation.
Rendered desktop workspace: sidebar history, calm chat canvas and first-class activity panel.
Rendered persisted long synthetic response scrolled to its generated-file cards; file titles and MIME details wrap within the viewport.
Rendered persisted synthetic response with inspectable MCP activity, measured fixture timings explicitly confined to test data, and four file cards.

observations: The actual mock backend generated four artifact cards with Gmail, Calendar and Drive sources and all four server namespaces.
A real browser artifact download completed and saved history restored after reload.
Rejecting the actual gated action created no send trace.
Creating a synthetic draft and sending that exact draft required two different approvals; the visible trace contained one send call.
Desktop, mobile, artifact library and approval captures in docs/demo/screenshots were inspected with view_image.
limits: No live Google or real LLM calls were performed.
Browser host required three missing Chromium libraries extracted into /tmp; this is documented in web/README.md.
